problems.title: Range of cosine on a closed interval
problems.question: Find the range of cosx for x∈[-π/3,π].
problems.idea: Check whether the input interval contains points giving both global extremes.
steps: Both 0 and π belong to the given interval, so the values 1 and -1 are attained.
Cosine is continuous, hence takes every value between them.
It never leaves [-1,1], so this is the exact range.

problems.title: Recognise a fifth-power binomial
problems.question: Factor 80a⁴b+32a⁵+80a³b²+40a²b³+10ab⁴+b⁵.
problems.idea: Compare the coefficients with the binomial expansion of (2a+b)⁵.
steps: Substitute u=2a and v=b.
The terms become 32a⁵,80a⁴b,80a³b²,40a²b³,10ab⁴,b⁵.
They are exactly the given terms, just written in a different order.

problems.title: Shape of a tilted section through a triangular prism
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has base side 4 and height 3. A plane through one base side makes 45° with the base. What shape is its nondegenerate section?
problems.idea: Compare the plane’s rise over the base altitude with the prism height.
formulas: A plane tilted by θ rises by distance·tanθ, measured perpendicular to its hinge.
steps: Use the chosen base side as the hinge. The opposite base vertex is distance 2√3 from it.
At that vertex’s horizontal position, the cutting plane would be height 2√3 tan45°=2√3>3.
Therefore it meets the top face before reaching the opposite vertical edge. The upper intersection is parallel to the hinge.
The prism and cut are symmetric about the perpendicular bisector of the hinge, so the remaining two sides have equal lengths.

problems.title: A midpoint perpendicular in a regular pyramid
problems.question: In a regular triangular pyramid, the perpendicular from base centre O to lateral edge MA has length 4 and bisects MA. Find the product of base circumradius OA and lateral edge MA.
problems.idea: In the right triangle MOA, the perpendicular bisector condition makes its two legs equal.
formulas: A point on a segment’s perpendicular bisector is equally distant from its endpoints.
For right-triangle legs R,R, hypotenuse is R√2 and altitude to it is R/√2.
steps: Let T be the midpoint of MA, with OT⊥MA and OT=4. Then OM=OA=R.
Because OM is the pyramid height, triangle MOA is right at O.
Its altitude to the hypotenuse is R/√2=4, giving R=4√2 and MA=8.
The product is OA·MA=4√2·8=32√2.

problems.title: Five-digit numbers using distinct even digits
problems.question: How many five-digit numbers have all digits even and different?
problems.idea: The five available digits must each be used once; the first digit cannot be zero.
formulas: Factorial n! counts arrangements of n different objects.
steps: Choose the first digit from 2,4,6,8: four choices.
Arrange the remaining four digits in 4!=24 ways.
The total is 4·24=96.

problems.title: Eight nonattacking rooks
problems.question: How many arrangements of eight identical rooks on an 8×8 chessboard have no two attacking each other?
problems.idea: Each row and each column must contain exactly one rook.
formulas: Two rooks attack along a common row or column.
A one-to-one assignment of eight rows to eight columns is a permutation.
steps: There are eight rooks and eight rows, with at most one per row, so each row has one.
The first row offers eight columns; subsequent rows offer 7,6,...,1 unused columns.

problems.title: Identify an impossible trigonometric inequality
problems.question: Which listed inequality has no solutions? One candidate is sin²x+cosx>1.5.
problems.idea: Find an upper bound for that candidate and check that the other inequalities each have an example.
steps: The candidate cannot exceed 1.25, so it cannot be greater than 1.5.
The other choices do have solutions: (x-1)²<7 at x=1; sin²x+sinx<2 at x=0; √x>-2 at x=0; x²>3 at x=2; sinx cosx<1 at x=0.
Therefore exactly the stated candidate has an empty solution set.

problems.title: Teams with both boys and girls
problems.question: Three boys and three girls form teams of at least three students, including at least one boy and one girl. How many teams are possible?
problems.idea: Count all subsets of size at least three and remove the two single-sex teams.
steps: There are choose(6,3)+choose(6,4)+choose(6,5)+choose(6,6)=20+15+6+1=42 teams of sufficient size.
A team of at least three containing only boys must be all three boys. Similarly there is only one all-girl team.
Remove those two: 42-2=40.

problems.title: Dihedral angle from total and lateral areas
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has total area 1.5 times its lateral area. Find the angle between a lateral face and the base.
problems.idea: Project the lateral faces onto the base.
formulas: Total area=base area B+lateral area L.
For a regular pyramid with common face inclination θ, B=Lcosθ.
steps: From B+L=1.5L obtain B=0.5L.
Each lateral face projects onto one of the three triangles from the base centre to a base side. Their projections cover the base.
Thus cosθ=B/L=1/2 and the acute dihedral angle is 60°.

problems.title: Cosine of an inverse tangent
problems.question: Express cos(arctanx) in terms of real x.
problems.idea: The principal arctangent always has positive cosine.
steps: Let θ=arctanx, so tanθ=x.
The identity gives cos²θ=1/(1+x²).
Cosθ>0 on the principal interval, so select the positive root.

problems.title: Consequences of a sine-square inequality
problems.question: If sin²x+sinx≤cos(π/2-x), which must hold: I sinx<-1/2, II cos⁴x=1, III cos²x+sinx=1?
problems.idea: Replace the complementary cosine by sinx.
steps: The inequality reduces to sin²x≤0.
A real square is nonnegative, so sinx=0 and cos²x=1.
I is false because 0 is not less than -1/2. II is true because cos⁴x=1. III is true because 1+0=1.

problems.title: A sine-cosine upper bound
problems.question: Solve sinx+cosx≤√2.
problems.idea: Write the sum as one sine with amplitude √2.
steps: The greatest possible value of the sum is √2.
The inequality allows equality, so even points achieving that maximum are included.
Every real x therefore satisfies it.

problems.title: Cosine between two three-dimensional vectors
problems.question: Find the cosine between a=(1,2,-1) and b=(-1,1,-2).
problems.idea: Use the dot product divided by the product of vector lengths.
steps: The dot product is -1+2+2=3.
Both squared lengths are 1+4+1=6.

problems.title: Add two binomial coefficients
problems.question: Find choose(10,2)+choose(10,3).
problems.idea: Evaluate directly or use Pascal’s identity.
steps: The sum is 45+120=165, also choose(11,3).

problems.title: Largest lateral face of a right-base pyramid
problems.question: A triangular pyramid has a right-triangle base with legs 3,4. The lateral faces containing the legs are perpendicular to the base, and the height is 1. Find its greatest lateral-face area.
problems.idea: The apex lies vertically above the right-angle vertex. Compare all three lateral faces.
formulas: For a 3–4–5 right triangle, altitude to the hypotenuse is 3·4/5=12/5.
steps: The faces over the two legs have areas 3·1/2=1.5 and 4·1/2=2.
The apex-to-hypotenuse distance is √(1+(12/5)²)=13/5.
The face over the hypotenuse has area 5·(13/5)/2=13/2=6.5.
This exceeds both other face areas.

problems.title: A non-strict sine inequality
problems.question: Solve sinx≤-√3/2.
problems.idea: Locate the arc at or below the horizontal level -√3/2.
steps: On one full turn [0,2π], sine is no greater than -√3/2 from 4π/3 to 5π/3.
Both endpoints are included because equality is allowed.
Add 2kπ to repeat this interval for every integer k.

problems.title: Assign two different council roles
problems.question: A ten-person council chooses a chair and a deputy. How many choices are possible?
problems.idea: The roles are different and must go to different people.
formulas: Ordered selections of two distinct people from n: n(n-1).
steps: There are ten choices for the chair.
After choosing the chair, nine people remain eligible to be deputy.
The multiplication rule gives 10·9=90 assignments.

problems.title: Length of a vector combination
problems.question: |a|=2, |b|=3, and the angle between them is 60°. Find |a+2b|.
problems.idea: Expand the squared length using the dot product.
steps: The squared length is 4+4·9+4·3=52.
Take the positive square root: √52=2√13.

problems.title: Exact tangent of fifteen degrees
problems.question: Find tan15°.
steps: Rationalise by multiplying top and bottom by √3-1.
The result is (4-2√3)/2=2-√3.

problems.title: Find a term in an eighth power
problems.question: Which listed term occurs in (x+2)⁸?
problems.idea: Use the binomial coefficient for the required power of x.
steps: For x⁶, set k=2. Its coefficient is choose(8,2)·4=28·4=112.
The other listed coefficients do not match: x⁸ has coefficient 1, x⁵ has 448, x⁴ has 1120, x³ has 1792, and x² has 1792.
Thus the listed valid term is 112x⁶.

problems.title: Complete spatial trapezoid coordinates
problems.question: Trapezoid ABCD has bases BC,AD. A=(1,2,3), B=(2,5,6), D=(2,3,4). Which listed C is possible?
problems.idea: The two base direction vectors must be parallel.
steps: AD=(1,1,1), so C must have the form (2+t,5+t,6+t).
Among the listed points, C=(6,9,10) gives t=4 in all three coordinates.
The positive multiple places the bases in the same direction and forms a nondegenerate trapezoid in the plane spanned by AB and AD.

problems.title: Identify a coplanar vector
problems.question: a=(2,3,1), b=(2,-3,1), and c is coplanar with them. Which listed c is possible?
problems.idea: Every linear combination of a,b has first coordinate twice its third.
steps: The vectors a,b are independent, and their span is the plane c1=2c3.
Of the listed options, only (2,4,1) satisfies this condition.
For confirmation, (2,4,1)=(7/6)a-(1/6)b.

problems.title: Count vertices from prism faces and edges
problems.question: A prism has 10 more edges than faces. How many vertices does it have?
problems.idea: Express all counts using the number n of sides in a base.
formulas: An n-gonal prism has edges E=3n, faces F=n+2, and vertices V=2n.
steps: The condition gives 3n-(n+2)=10.
Thus 2n-2=10, so n=6.
The prism has V=2n=12 vertices.

problems.title: Angle between two vectors in a cube
problems.question: M,N are the midpoints of A1B1,C1D1 in cube ABCDA1B1C1D1. Find the angle between AM and CN.
problems.idea: Coordinates remove the need to interpret the apparent angle in a drawing.
steps: Then AM=(1/2,0,1) and CN=(-1/2,0,1). Their dot product is 3/4.
Each squared length is 5/4, so cosθ=(3/4)/(5/4)=3/5. A different cube size cancels from the ratio.

problems.title: An axial section of a square-pyramid frustum
problems.question: A square-pyramid frustum has base side lengths 2,6 and slant height 5. Find its axial-section area.
problems.idea: For the intended central section through opposite side midpoints, first find the vertical height.
steps: The horizontal offset between corresponding side midpoints is (6-2)/2=2.
The vertical height is h=√(25-4)=√21.
The midpoint axial section has parallel sides 2 and 6, giving area (2+6)√21/2=4√21.
problems.note: This uses a regular square frustum and the conventional midpoint section. A diagonal axial plane instead gives area 4√42. In a square frustum, “through the axis” alone does not uniquely specify the plane’s orientation.
